changes: Started as three LOW cleanups and grew, through four review-driven scope expansions, into a durable audit guarantee. (1) transition-orchestrator.ts: buildPhaseTransitionProcessEvent gained optional transitionType/reason appended only when defined, and the call site passes them only when eventType==='REOPEN', so a gated PLAN->INIT reopen leaves its operator reason in the append-only phase_transition event while normal transitions keep a byte-identical shape. (2) Same file: the REOPEN checklist-reset comment now states its real guarantee (concurrency-atomic via the mkdir persist claim, ordered phase-write-last) instead of 'land together or not at all'. (3) worktree.ts: the pruneWorktreeRegistry comment documents that `git worktree prune --expire now` cannot remove a live sibling, is repo-wide not story-scoped, and that a locked worktree survives even with its directory gone. (4) process-fact-registry.ts + scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs: the reopen audit semantics are DECLARED and MECHANICALLY ASSERTED, satisfying the dual-layer process-fact contract so the guarantee cannot be silently refactored away. (5) The reopen audit record now lands in the SAME atomic writeStory rename as phase=INIT, with reconcilePendingReopenAudit at the top of every transition, so a crash between the phase write and the event append is recoverable rather than an unaudited reopen. (6) reconcileReopenAuditBeforeOutOfBandPhaseChange rescues the record at the two out-of-band phase mutators (story_discard in worktree.ts, zombie DONE repair in story-query.ts), reading from the doomed worktree copy and appending to the surviving log. (7) types.ts declares the pendingReopenAudit recovery field. plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.ts now carries 6 fault-injection drills.
usage: lattice story_advance '{"storyId":"B-xxxx","phase":"INIT","reason":"why the frozen title must change"}' from PLAN. The reason is then durably readable in .lattice/story/actives/B-xxxx/process-events.jsonl as a phase_transition event with transitionType=reopen. `npm run test:process-fact-contract` mechanically enforces the semantics; a crash mid-transition is reconciled on the next transition, and story_discard / story_reconcile rescue the record before destroying it.
expectedOutcome: A maintainer who reopens a story to INIT can always prove WHY afterwards: the reason survives a crash between the phase write and the event append, survives a story_discard that deletes the worktree holding it, and cannot be silently refactored away because the process-fact contract fails if the marker or reason is dropped.
actualTranscript: npm --prefix packages/main run build -> exit 0. node packages/main/dist/tasks/plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.js -> 6 drills pass incl. '✓ same-reason reopens are audited separately' (exit 0). node packages/main/dist/tasks/flow-stability-smoke.js -> '✓ flow stability smoke passed'. npm run test:process-fact-contract -> 'Process fact contract verified'. done_required_validate -> PASS (packages/main build exit 0 + root full `npm test` exit 0). grep -c 'land together or not at all' transition-orchestrator.ts -> 0. grep -c 'live sibling' worktree.ts -> 2. RED PROOFS, each in an isolated scratch copy and each COMPILING CLEAN under tsc (so this class is provably not catchable by the build): F-003 7 mutations, F-004 12/13 mutations, F-005 11/11 mutations, round-5 8 mutations — every one flipped the contract or smoke to exit 1 and reverting restored exit 0.
outcomeDiff: The delivered scope is MUCH larger than requested, entirely because independent review found real defects. The original ask was three LOW cleanups (deliverables 1-3). Deliverables 4-7 were added after: an independent cross-host reviewer (codex-host-b) returned FAIL twice, first for missing process-fact registration (F-003) and then for the audit event being appended after the phase write and after the persist claim was released, leaving an UNRECOVERABLE unaudited reopen (F-004); then a behavior reviewer proved the resulting invariant was still falsifiable via story_discard (F-005). Notably the main agent had explicitly and WRONGLY argued the F-004 class of concern was merely a pre-existing universal property and excluded it from scope — the requester had asked for exactly this in their original section 5, and they were right. Two deviations from the original request remain deliberate: actor/eventId provenance excluded per scope-boundary.json after the requester answered 'no preference'; and full crash-transactionality was not achieved (the window is made RECOVERABLE, not eliminated).
limitations: The audit event records reason/transitionType/fromPhase/toPhase/timestamp but NOT actor or eventId. The two-write window is made RECOVERABLE, not eliminated: after a crash the reason is durable immediately and only the event can be late. Recovery fires on transitions plus the two out-of-band phase mutators, NOT on arbitrary read-only commands (store.readStory is outside this story's scope). The already-audited check is read-then-append rather than atomic CAS, serialized by the per-story transition lock, so its failure mode is a duplicate event sharing one auditId (dedupable), never a lost one. The doomed copy's record is deliberately not cleared, to avoid dirtying a worktree that a non-force discard would then refuse. story_discard --purge removes the log including the rescued event — an explicit erase, now warned about. No `lattice doctor` orphaned-record check was added because doctor's file was outside scope; that remains a real advisory gap. The registry entry is audit-only history, NOT gate evidence — no gate consumes transitionType or reason.
pitfalls: Six lessons. (1) Driving lattice from a NESTED git worktree makes INIT_CHECK's reconcile resolve a double-nested path and die with a misleading 'spawnSync git ENOENT'; it split story metadata across two branches and needed cherry-picking to recover. (2) The validate suite is 51 commands and exceeds story_advance's 900s watchdog; every TEST/DONE advance needs LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS raised. (3) Pre-writing a 'reference implementation' before dispatching implementers is a trap — independent implementers found real defects in ALL THREE original commits. (4) verification_evidence_refresh_stale will rebind ANY stale evidence including one whose command was the DESTRUCTIVE 'git worktree prune --expire now -v' and one using a moving 'git diff HEAD~1'; re-run evidence commands yourself before refreshing. (5) CLOSEOUT ORDERING: every metadata auto-commit moves materialHash and stales evidence, delivery-check and the assurance floor — update summary.json BEFORE the delivery reviewer signs, and bind the floor LAST. (6) THE BIG ONE: the local Claude reviewer panel passed a MAJOR defect across TWO rounds and a second MAJOR defect across FOUR; both were caught only by the independent cross-host reviewer, and a third by a reviewer role not in the default roster. Do not treat local-panel consensus as sufficient for a load-bearing guarantee. Also: a naive fix for F-005 would have been a silent no-op, because cli/runtime-root.ts redirects story_discard's root away from the worktree holding the record — always verify the fix actually executes on the path it claims to protect.
